evidence: Figure 6: An overview of existing parameter-efficient finetuning (PEFT) methods.
Green boxes show the operators of the backbone LLM, while blue boxes are the operators introduced by different PEFT methods.
Figure 6 illustrates examples of how various PEFT methods attach their bypass networks to the base LLM.

summary: Figure 6 from FlexLLM compares the operator-level architecture of three parameter-efficient finetuning (PEFT) methods -- LoRA, Adapters, and (IA)^3 -- against the plain backbone Transformer. Each of the four panels draws the same base pipeline (Layer Norm, three Linear projections, Matmul/Softmax attention, Add, another Layer Norm, and an SiLU-gated MLP block) in green boxes labelled LLM Backbone Operators. Blue boxes labelled PEFT Operators show the extra Linear/ReLU/Multiply layers each method attaches to the backbone. Solid gray/blue arrows mark activations that must be reserved for backpropagation; light dashed arrows mark activations that can be pruned because no PEFT operator depends on them. The figure's purpose is to justify FlexLLM's per-PEFT-method activation-reservation analysis used for memory-efficient co-serving.
summary_zh: 图6对比了LoRA、Adapters和(IA)^3等参数高效微调方法与原始Transformer骨干网络的算子级结构，绿色为骨干算子，蓝色为PEFT算子，实线箭头表示需保留的反向传播激活，虚线箭头表示可裁剪的激活。
